question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x)))+(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x)))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡(x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(x))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x)^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))^{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sec}⁡(x))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(x))\end{aligned}
$$
